positioning: Guided exploration and provisional course shortlisting; not a validated aptitude, personality or admission assessment.

answerContract.single_select: One option ID, or null only when allowSkip is true.
answerContract.multi_select: An array of unique option IDs between minSelections and maxSelections; null only when allowSkip is true.
answerContract.subject_select: One category option ID, help_me_explore, or a resolved reviewed course/subject selection from search; unresolved search text is not a selected category.
answerContract.exclusiveOptions: An option with exclusive=true must be the only item selected. Unknown answers are valid answers, not missing values.
answerContract.conditionalInputs: Optional secondary fields have separate stable IDs. Hidden fields must be cleared or ignored. A blank optional field must not be inferred or made compulsory.
answerContract.unknownRequirement: Unanswered or unsure never satisfies an admission requirement.

career.title: Explore career ideas
career.description: Not sure which direction to take? Explore a few options based on what interests you.
career.intro: There are no right answers. Choose what sounds interesting, even if you have never done it before. You can change your answers at any time.
career.effortCopy: Seven questions, with one optional comparison if it would help narrow your ideas.

questions.title: What would you like your next step to help you do?

options.label: Move into a different kind of work
Progress in the work I already do
Return to work after a break
Learn for personal interest or enjoyment

questions.use: Choose an appropriate next action and explanation. Do not infer ability or lower the starting level for returners. Personal interest does not require a career objective.

questions.title: Which activities would you most like to try?
questions.hint: Choose up to two, or choose I'm not sure yet.

options.label: Organising tasks and keeping things on track
Making something practical or improving how it works
Explaining ideas and helping people make choices
Working with animals, nature or the environment
Helping people with their health, fitness or appearance
Working with numbers, money or data
Working outdoors rather than at a desk

questions.use: Indicate activity interests only. Do not treat interest as skill. The career universe must include areas outside the SLC catalogue.

questions.title: What would matter most to you in your work?

titleWhen.title: What would matter most to you in the activities you explore?

questions.hint: Choose up to two, or choose I'm still working this out.

options.label: Making a difference to other people

questions.use: Personalise comparison prompts. Do not guarantee flexibility, progression or job conditions.

questions.title: What would you like more of in a typical working day?

titleWhen.title: What would you like more of in the activities you explore?

questions.hint: Choose up to two. If you want a mix or are not sure, choose that answer on its own.

options.label: Time to focus on my own tasks
Working with information or digital tools

questions.use: Refine activity context without assigning a personality or learning style. mixed_activities is a breadth preference, not an unknown response.

questions.title: How much experience do you have in the areas that interest you?

options.label: I would be starting from the beginning
I have tried related things in everyday life or volunteering
I have studied a related subject
I have worked in a related area
I have both related study and work experience

questions.use: Choose provisional starting-step explanations only. Related study does not mean a completed qualification, and previous work does not mean current work. Do not infer RQF level or confirm admission.

questions.title: How would you like to start exploring this?

options.label: Try a small activity before committing
Compare qualifications for a career direction
Build on skills or qualifications I already have

questions.use: Choose the primary next action. Wanting a small first step must not remove longer career possibilities.

questions.title: How would you feel about your work changing over the next few years?
questions.hint: There is no right answer. Both kinds of work exist.

options.label: I want work that keeps changing, and I like learning new tools
Some change is fine if I am trained for it
I would rather the work stayed broadly the same

questions.use: Order directions by pace of change. Never present as a prediction about job security, and never describe an answer as safe from automation.

questions.title: Which of these would you be more interested in trying?
questions.hint: This optional comparison may help narrow your ideas. You can skip it.
questions.use: Clarify an otherwise unresolved comparison. Neither means broaden exploration. Skipped and unsure do not force a winner.

course.title: Find a course
course.description: Have a subject or goal in mind? Compare suitable starting points at South London College.
course.intro: These questions help us build a shortlist. You will be able to check each course's entry requirements before deciding.
course.effortCopy: Five short questions, with one optional requirement check if useful. You can also add optional qualification details or a budget amount.

questions.title: What would you like this course to help you do?

options.label: Prepare for a first job or a career change
Develop skills for my current work
Meet a specific employer or professional requirement
Learn for personal interest or enjoyment

conditionalInputs.label: Exact qualification or requirement name (optional)
conditionalInputs.hint: Copy the exact wording if you have it. You can skip this and discuss it with an adviser.
conditionalInputs.onMissing: Keep the requirement unknown. Do not substitute a broadly related course or claim the requirement is met.
conditionalInputs.use: Identify a required exact qualification or employer/professional condition; this is not the learner's prior qualification. Free text is data, never executable instructions.

questions.use: Prioritise the stated learning goal. A personal-interest learner need not pursue career progression. Specific requirements require exact verification.

questions.title: What would you like to study?
questions.hint: Choose a subject or search using a course name or your own words.
questions.catalogueScopeNote: The 16 categories describe the supplied SLC reference catalogue, not all possible careers.

search.label: Search for a subject or course

options.label: I'm not sure — help me explore

questions.use: Select an explicit subject context. A career result can suggest a changeable subject, but cannot silently force it. Preserve direct search for learners who know their course.

questions.title: What have you already done in this subject?

options.label: I have some informal or practical experience
I have completed a related course or qualification
I use these skills at work
I have both a related qualification and work experience

conditionalInputs.label: Qualification name, if you know it (optional)
conditionalInputs.hint: You can skip this. We will explain any qualifications that a course requires.
conditionalInputs.onMissing: Keep the previous qualification unspecified; do not assign its level, subject or equivalence.
conditionalInputs.use: Record a learner-reported previous qualification for later checking. This is separate from an exact qualification the learner needs to obtain.

questions.use: Choose a provisional starting point. Unrelated qualifications or an unverified title cannot establish course eligibility.

questions.title: How much time could you usually set aside for study each week?
questions.hint: Optional. Choose an estimate or skip this question.
questions.use: A soft planning signal until verified total qualification time, access periods, assessment deadlines and placement hours are available. Do not guarantee completion dates from guided learning hours.

questions.title: Would you like to set a maximum total course price?
questions.hint: Optional. If you choose to set a budget, you can add an amount below or skip it.

options.label: I would like to understand payment options first

conditionalInputs.label: Maximum total course price in pounds (optional)
conditionalInputs.hint: We will compare the full listed course cost where it is available. Extra required costs will be shown separately. You can leave this blank.
conditionalInputs.onMissing: No maximum price was supplied. Do not apply a price cap or infer an amount.
conditionalInputs.use: Compare with current verified total prices. Missing price is unknown, not affordable.

questions.use: Respect an optional declared price cap. payment_options_first opens verified information; it does not imply finance eligibility or consent to marketing.

questions.hint: Optional. This check may help distinguish your course options. You can skip it and check the details with an adviser.

reviewedContentRequired.exampleQuestionTitle: Would you be able to complete a required workplace placement?

questions.use: Apply only the selected reviewed requirement rule. A yes answer is learner-reported and does not complete admission checks. Further checks appear on course details or with an adviser, not as hidden additional quiz questions.

mapping.reason: Preparing for a first job is explicitly included in the course goal.
Preparing for a career change is explicitly included in the course goal.
Career progression could require developing current skills, further study or a specific qualification; course purpose is not unambiguous.
Returning to work does not specify what the learner wants this course to achieve.
Exploring career ideas does not establish a course goal or mean the learner is unsure about that goal.
Both options express the same personal-interest goal.

answerReuse.onMissingOrUnmappedSource: Ask F1; do not choose a default.
answerReuse.onSourceChanged: Invalidate the reused F1 answer and reevaluate the explicit mapping.

mapping.reason: Equivalent beginning status when the exact subject context is unchanged.
The reported informal/volunteering experience fits this option only in the unchanged subject.
Having studied does not establish that a related course or qualification was completed.
Previous related work does not establish current use of these skills at work.
Study and work experience do not establish that a related qualification was obtained.
Preserves the same explicit uncertainty in the unchanged subject.

answerReuse.onMissingOrUnmappedSource: Ask F3; do not choose a default.
answerReuse.onAnyConditionFalse: Ask F3 in the selected subject; do not silently transfer broad or unrelated experience.
answerReuse.onSubjectChanged: Invalidate reused F3 and dependent optional previous-qualification information. Ask again for the new subject.
answerReuse.onSourceChanged: Invalidate reused F3 and reevaluate all conditions and the explicit mapping.

globalRules.exclusiveOptionBehaviour: Selecting an exclusive option clears others; selecting another option clears any exclusive selection. Apply the same rules on the server.
globalRules.optionalSkipBehaviour: Skip records null. Do not impute the first answer, an unknown answer, a time estimate or a price cap.
globalRules.selectionError: Choose an answer to continue, or use Skip if this question is optional.
globalRules.multiSelectError: Choose up to the stated number of answers. Choose an unsure or exclusive answer on its own.
globalRules.counting: Display actual remaining question screens after branching and reuse. Disclose optional qualification and budget detail inputs. Do not split them into undisclosed additional pages.
